evidence_items.publisher: Quanta Computer Inc., hosted by Taiwan Stock Exchange
evidence_items.locator: Pages 3–5: quarterly income statement, annual income statement and balance sheet; quoted sentence is the accounting-basis footnote

receipt.public_excerpt: Financial figures were Taiwan IFRSs based.

evidence_items.explanation: The balance-sheet table reports inventory of NT$512,946 million versus NT$334,618 million at September 30, a 53.3% increase; these are not USD figures. The income tables give Q4 margins of 6.33% versus 7.45%, while 7.0% versus 7.9% belongs to the annual comparison.

evidence_items.publisher: Quanta Computer Inc., hosted by Singapore Exchange
evidence_items.locator: Note 4(8), inventory valuation policy; Note 6(7), page 35, inventory composition and comparative balances

receipt.public_excerpt: 存貨係以成本與淨變現價值孰低衡量。

evidence_items.explanation: The quoted policy measures inventory at the lower of cost and net realizable value; Note 6(7) reports NT$512,945,798 thousand versus NT$261,886,319 thousand, a 95.9% increase. Raw materials increased while finished goods decreased, but the note does not identify GPUs separately.

receipt.public_excerpt: FY2025 gross margin was 7.0%, compared to 7.9% in FY2024.

evidence_items.explanation: This correctly identifies the percentages as annual margins, consistent with the original presentation. It establishes a period-label problem in the ancillary margin assertion, not a contradiction of the inventory metric.

unresolved_gaps: The exchange rates and conversion dates behind $10.54 billion, $16.3 billion and $8.33 billion were not established.
No GPU-specific inventory valuation, aging schedule or installation-delay disclosure was found.
The exact wording combines an inventory assertion with a quarterly margin comparison, while the normalized proposition emphasizes GPU accumulation.
